we have developed a novel methodology for rapid and high-resolution detection of small (40 kb and up) constitutional deletions, which we applied to a large series of neurofibromatose type 2 ( NF2) patients and found that deletions are more frequent in severe and moderate than mild patients, but do not correlate with any other clinical feature.
the frequency and extent (i.e., size) of constitutional deletions in the 22q12 region of NF2 patients is not related to the clinical phenotype.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deletion frequency in NF2 is 20-30%.
NF2 deletions occur in 10.3% of patients with severe, 16.7% of patients with moderate and 9.1% of patients with mild NF2.
the frequency of constitutional NF2 deletions in NF2 patients is not correlated with the disease severity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NF2 gene is not the only determinant of the clinical outcome of the disease.
array-CGH is an efficient tool to screen for deletions, and that the NF2 gene does not play a major role in the clinical heterogeneity of the disease.
we have identified deletions in 24% of the patients with a wide variety of phenotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the array-CGH technique is a powerful tool that is able to provide a high resolution deletion map in a single experiment.
the array-CGH technology can be applied to a variety of clinical and biological samples, and can be used to rapidly detect small deletions and duplications.
the array-CGH technology can be used to detect deletions of the entire NF2 gene in NF2 patients.
